## env.example

````text
# =============================================================================
# MailFlow — Environment Variables Reference
# =============================================================================
# Copy this file to .env and fill in your values.
# NEVER commit .env to Git.
# =============================================================================

# ── Database ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DB_URL=jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/mailflow
DB_USERNAME=mailflow
DB_PASSWORD=your-database-password-here

# ── Redis ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
REDIS_HOST=localhost
REDIS_PORT=6379
REDIS_PASSWORD=
# Hosted Redis (Upstash) needs TLS:
REDIS_SSL=false

# ── RabbitMQ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RABBITMQ_HOST=localhost
RABBITMQ_PORT=5672
RABBITMQ_USERNAME=guest
RABBITMQ_PASSWORD=guest
# Hosted RabbitMQ (CloudAMQP): virtual host = your user name, port 5671 with TLS.
RABBITMQ_VHOST=/
RABBITMQ_SSL=false

# ── SMTP ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Full guide: docs/EMAIL_SMTP_SETUP.md
#
# For development, use MailHog (default). No credentials required.
SMTP_HOST=localhost
SMTP_PORT=1025
SMTP_USERNAME=
SMTP_PASSWORD=
SMTP_AUTH=false
SMTP_TLS=false

# For REAL delivery with Gmail (free): requires 2-Step Verification + a
# Google App Password (NOT your normal Gmail password). Also set
# EMAIL_MODE=production below. NEVER commit the app password to Git.
# SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com
# SMTP_PORT=587
# SMTP_USERNAME=your@gmail.com
# SMTP_PASSWORD=your-16-char-google-app-password
# SMTP_AUTH=true
# SMTP_TLS=true

# For Brevo (used by the hosted deployment, see docs/DEPLOYMENT.md):
# SMTP_HOST=smtp-relay.brevo.com
# SMTP_PORT=587
# SMTP_USERNAME=<your Brevo SMTP login, e.g. 1234abc@smtp-brevo.com>
# SMTP_PASSWORD=<your Brevo SMTP key>
# SMTP_AUTH=true
# SMTP_TLS=true
# EMAIL_FROM_POLICY=platform
# EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS=<a sender verified in Brevo>

# Optional SMTP tuning (sensible defaults applied if unset):
# SMTP_SSL_TRUST=            # e.g. smtp.gmail.com if the JVM trust store needs it
# SMTP_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS=10000
# SMTP_READ_TIMEOUT_MS=10000
# SMTP_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS=10000

# ── Email ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Set to 'production' to use real SMTP, 'development' to log to console.
# NOTE: when EMAIL_MODE=production AND SMTP_AUTH=true, the app validates at
# startup that SMTP_HOST/SMTP_USERNAME/SMTP_PASSWORD are set and fails fast
# with a clear error if any are missing.
EMAIL_MODE=development
# With Gmail, the actual From is forced to SMTP_USERNAME (Gmail rewrites it
# anyway); EMAIL_FROM_NAME is still used as the display name and the campaign's
# configured sender becomes the Reply-To.
EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS=noreply@yourdomain.com
EMAIL_FROM_NAME=MailFlow
EMAIL_RATE_LIMIT=100
# Which address goes in From with authenticated SMTP: smtp-username (Gmail) or
# platform (EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS; for Brevo/SES, whose login is not an email address).
EMAIL_FROM_POLICY=smtp-username

# ── JWT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# IMPORTANT: Generate a secure random secret for production!
# Example: openssl rand -base64 64
JWT_SECRET=your-very-long-and-secure-jwt-secret-at-least-256-bits

# ── Production ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod turns on a start-up check that refuses unsafe settings
# (default JWT secret, demo accounts enabled, FRONTEND_URL missing).
# SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod
# The seeded demo accounts below have public passwords: false on any public deployment.
DEMO_ACCOUNTS_ENABLED=true
# Database connections (hosted free databases allow few: use 5).
# DB_POOL_SIZE=20

# ── Batch ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
BATCH_CHUNK_SIZE=50
BATCH_MAX_RETRIES=3
BATCH_SKIP_LIMIT=100
BATCH_THROTTLE_LIMIT=4

# ── AI-assisted email drafting (optional) ───────────────────────────────────────
# AI is OFF by default. When disabled or no API key is set, the AI endpoints
# return a clear 503 and the rest of MailFlow works normally.
# Provider is "gemini" (default) or "openai".
AI_ENABLED=false
AI_PROVIDER=gemini

# Google Gemini (Generative Language API). Get a key from Google AI Studio:
# https://aistudio.google.com/apikey  — NEVER commit a real key.
GEMINI_API_KEY=
GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-1.5-flash
# GEMINI_BASE_URL=https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta
# GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30

# OpenAI (alternative provider; only used when AI_PROVIDER=openai)
OPENAI_API_KEY=
OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini

# ── Application ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
APP_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080
SERVER_PORT=8080
UPLOAD_DIR=./uploads
MAX_ATTACHMENT_MB=10

# ── Deployment URLs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# BACKEND_URL  — public base URL of the API (used in docs / links).
# FRONTEND_URL — public URL(s) of the deployed frontend. Added to the backend
#                CORS allow-list. Comma-separated for multiple origins.
#                Local dev origins (3000/5173) are always allowed automatically.
BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8080
FRONTEND_URL=http://localhost:3000

# =============================================================================
# DEMO CREDENTIALS (local development only; disabled when DEMO_ACCOUNTS_ENABLED=false)
# =============================================================================
# Admin:            admin@mailflow.local       / Admin@123
# Campaign Manager: manager@mailflow.local     / Manager@123
# Viewer:           viewer@mailflow.local      / Viewer@123
````

## github/workflows/ci.yml

````yaml
name: MailFlow CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, develop ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  # ── Backend ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  backend:
    name: Backend (Java 21 / Maven)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_DB: mailflow_test
          POSTGRES_USER: mailflow
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: mailflow
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up JDK 21
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          java-version: '21'
          distribution: 'temurin'
          cache: maven

      - name: Build and run unit tests
        run: mvn clean verify -B -Dspring.profiles.active=test
        env:
          DB_URL: jdbc:h2:mem:testdb
          JWT_SECRET: ci-test-secret-key-at-least-256-bits-long-for-tests
          REDIS_HOST: localhost
          RABBITMQ_HOST: localhost

      - name: Publish test report
        uses: dorny/test-reporter@v1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: Backend Tests
          path: target/surefire-reports/*.xml
          reporter: java-junit

      - name: Build Docker image (verify Dockerfile)
        run: docker build -t mailflow-backend:ci .
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'

  # ── Frontend ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  frontend:
    name: Frontend (Node 20 / Vite)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node 20
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
          cache: 'npm'
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Type check
        run: npx tsc --noEmit

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint || true   # non-blocking; enforce separately

      - name: Build production bundle
        run: npm run build
        env:
          VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:8080

      - name: Verify build output
        run: ls -lh dist/

  # ── Security scan ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  security:
    name: Security Scan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [backend, frontend]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Restore the SAME Maven cache the backend job saved (key derived from pom.xml),
      # so Trivy can resolve Java dependencies from the local ~/.m2 repository offline.
      - name: Set up JDK 21 (restore Maven cache)
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          java-version: '21'
          distribution: 'temurin'
          cache: maven

      # PRIMARY COVERAGE MITIGATION (not an absolute guarantee).
      # Trivy's offline pom scan can only analyze dependencies already present in the
      # local ~/.m2 repository. Per aquasecurity/trivy#10691, when Trivy cannot resolve
      # a dependency (e.g. remote 429) it soft-skips it and the scan can still report
      # success — Trivy does NOT reliably enumerate what it skipped. Maven, by contrast,
      # fails loudly when it cannot resolve the dependency/plugin graph. We therefore
      # resolve the graph with Maven FIRST and fail the job on any unresolved artifact.
      # Caveat: this strongly mitigates silent under-reporting but is not a 100%
      # guarantee — Maven's resolve goals do not necessarily walk the exact same
      # transitive set Trivy parses from pom.xml, and a dependency with an
      # undeterminable version still has its children skipped by Trivy by design.
      - name: Resolve Maven dependency graph into local repo (coverage mitigation)
        id: maven_resolve
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          if mvn -B -ntp dependency:go-offline \
                         dependency:resolve \
                         dependency:resolve-plugins 2>&1 | tee mvn-resolve.log; then
            echo "resolved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "resolved=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::error::Maven could not resolve the full dependency/plugin graph — the local cache is INCOMPLETE, so an offline Trivy scan would silently under-report."
            if grep -Eiq "status code: 429|Too Many Requests" mvn-resolve.log; then
              echo "::error::Maven Central returned HTTP 429 (rate limited). Aborting rather than producing a silently-incomplete security scan (see aquasecurity/trivy#10691)."
            fi
            exit 1
          fi
          # Informational only — a non-empty local repo, NOT a proof of complete coverage.
          echo "Local ~/.m2 .pom count (informational only): $(find ~/.m2/repository -name '*.pom' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"

      - name: Run Trivy vulnerability scanner (offline Maven resolution)
        id: trivy
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        with:
          scan-type: 'fs'
          scan-ref: '.'
          scanners: 'vuln,secret,misconfig'   # preserve vulnerability, secret AND misconfig scanning
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
          format: 'json'
          output: 'trivy-report.json'
          exit-code: '0'   # Non-blocking for now; set to '1' to block on critical findings
        env:
          # Resolve Java dependencies from the local ~/.m2 repo only — never contact Maven Central.
          TRIVY_OFFLINE_SCAN: true

      # Post-scan report. Runs even if the Trivy step failed (if: always()), but it
      # does NOT convert a failed scan into a success — it fails when Maven resolution
      # failed or when Trivy did not produce a report. It distinguishes four facts:
      #   (1) whether Maven dependency resolution succeeded,
      #   (2) whether Trivy produced a report,
      #   (3) how many Java packages were discovered,
      #   (4) coverage limitations that cannot be auto-verified.
      - name: Report security scan coverage
        if: always()
        run: |
          fail=0

          # (1) Maven dependency resolution outcome.
          if [ "${{ steps.maven_resolve.outputs.resolved }}" = "true" ]; then
            echo "Maven dependency resolution: SUCCEEDED (local ~/.m2 populated)"
          else
            echo "Maven dependency resolution: FAILED or did not run"
            fail=1
          fi

          # (2) Did Trivy produce a report, and is it valid JSON? Also honor the step outcome.
          report_valid=0
          if [ -f trivy-report.json ]; then
            if jq -e . trivy-report.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Trivy report: PRESENT and valid JSON (trivy-report.json)"
              report_valid=1
            else
              echo "::error::trivy-report.json is present but is NOT valid JSON — cannot verify scan coverage."
              fail=1
            fi
          else
            echo "Trivy report: MISSING — the scan did not complete successfully"
            fail=1
          fi
          if [ "${{ steps.trivy.outcome }}" = "failure" ]; then
            echo "Trivy step outcome: FAILURE"
            fail=1
          fi

          # (3) Evidence from the report (only parsed when the JSON is valid).
          #     Distinguishes "scan completed" from "no CRITICAL/HIGH vulnerabilities".
          if [ "$report_valid" -eq 1 ]; then
            PKGS=$(jq '[.Results[]? | select(.Class=="lang-pkgs") | (.Packages // []) | length] | add // 0' trivy-report.json)
            echo "Scan status: COMPLETED (a completed scan does NOT by itself mean the project is vulnerability-free)."
            echo "Java/lang packages analyzed by Trivy (offline): ${PKGS:-0}"
            jq -r '.Results[]? | select(.Class=="lang-pkgs") | "  target=\(.Target) type=\(.Type) packages=\((.Packages // []) | length)"' trivy-report.json || true
            # Report the ACTUAL CRITICAL/HIGH finding count. exit-code is 0 (non-blocking)
            # for now, so findings do NOT fail the job — they must be read here, not inferred
            # from a green checkmark.
            VULNS=$(jq '[.Results[]? | (.Vulnerabilities // [])[]] | length' trivy-report.json)
            echo "CRITICAL/HIGH vulnerabilities reported by Trivy: ${VULNS:-0}"
            if [ "${VULNS:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "::warning::Trivy reported ${VULNS} CRITICAL/HIGH vulnerability finding(s). The job is GREEN only because exit-code=0 (non-blocking); review the findings in the scan output."
            fi
            if [ "${PKGS:-0}" -eq 0 ]; then
              echo "::warning::Trivy analyzed 0 Java packages — coverage is likely incomplete; investigate before trusting the result."
            fi
          fi

          # (4) Coverage limitations that cannot be verified automatically.
          echo "Coverage limitation: Trivy does not reliably enumerate dependencies it"
          echo "  silently skips (aquasecurity/trivy#10691), so a clean Trivy result alone"
          echo "  does NOT prove complete coverage. Trust requires BOTH: Maven resolution"
          echo "  succeeded above AND a plausible package count. Otherwise review logs manually."

          if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::Security scan did not complete with verifiable coverage (see facts above)."
            exit 1
          fi
````

## docker-compose.yml

````yaml
version: "3.9"

# =============================================================================
# MailFlow — Complete local development stack
#
# Services:
#   postgres   — PostgreSQL 16 database
#   redis      — Redis 7 for rate limiting + caching
#   rabbitmq   — RabbitMQ 3 with management UI
#   mailhog    — Fake SMTP server (dev email capture)
#   backend    — Spring Boot application
#   frontend   — React dashboard (Vite dev server)
#
# Start: docker compose up
# Stop:  docker compose down
# Reset: docker compose down -v
# =============================================================================

services:

  # ── PostgreSQL ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: mailflow-postgres
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: mailflow
      POSTGRES_USER: mailflow
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: mailflow
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U mailflow -d mailflow"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  # ── Redis ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: mailflow-redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3

  # ── RabbitMQ ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  rabbitmq:
    image: rabbitmq:3.13-management-alpine
    container_name: mailflow-rabbitmq
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER: guest
      RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS: guest
    ports:
      - "5672:5672"    # AMQP
      - "15672:15672"  # Management UI → http://localhost:15672
    volumes:
      - rabbitmq_data:/var/lib/rabbitmq
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "rabbitmq-diagnostics", "ping"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5

  # ── MailHog (Fake SMTP) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  mailhog:
    image: mailhog/mailhog:latest
    container_name: mailflow-mailhog
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "1025:1025"  # SMTP
      - "8025:8025"  # Web UI → http://localhost:8025
    logging:
      driver: none

  # ── Backend ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  backend:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    container_name: mailflow-backend
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      rabbitmq:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      # Database
      DB_URL: jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/mailflow
      DB_USERNAME: mailflow
      DB_PASSWORD: mailflow
      # Redis
      REDIS_HOST: redis
      REDIS_PORT: 6379
      # RabbitMQ
      RABBITMQ_HOST: rabbitmq
      RABBITMQ_PORT: 5672
      RABBITMQ_USERNAME: guest
      RABBITMQ_PASSWORD: guest
      # SMTP (MailHog)
      SMTP_HOST: mailhog
      SMTP_PORT: 1025
      SMTP_AUTH: "false"
      SMTP_TLS: "false"
      # Email config
      EMAIL_MODE: development
      EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS: noreply@mailflow.local
      EMAIL_FROM_NAME: MailFlow
      EMAIL_RATE_LIMIT: 100
      # JWT — CHANGE IN PRODUCTION
      JWT_SECRET: change-me-in-production-must-be-at-least-256-bits-long
      # Batch
      BATCH_CHUNK_SIZE: 50
      BATCH_MAX_RETRIES: 3
      # AI (disabled by default)
      AI_ENABLED: "false"
      OPENAI_API_KEY: ""
      # App
      APP_BASE_URL: http://localhost:8080
      SERVER_PORT: 8080
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      - uploads:/app/uploads

  # ── Frontend ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  frontend:
    build:
      context: ./frontend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    container_name: mailflow-frontend
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - backend
    environment:
      VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:8080
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"

volumes:
  postgres_data:
  redis_data:
  rabbitmq_data:
  uploads:
````

## Dockerfile

````dockerfile
# =============================================================================
# MailFlow Backend — Multi-stage Docker build
# Stage 1: Build with Maven (maven image includes Maven + JDK 21)
# Stage 2: Minimal JRE runtime
# =============================================================================

# ── Stage 1: Build ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM maven:3.9.6-eclipse-temurin-21-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# Cache dependency layer separately from source code
COPY pom.xml .
RUN mvn dependency:go-offline -B --no-transfer-progress || true

# Copy source and build — tests run in CI, skip here
COPY src ./src
RUN mvn clean package -DskipTests -B --no-transfer-progress

# ── Stage 2: Runtime ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine AS runtime

# Non-root user for security
RUN addgroup -S mailflow && adduser -S mailflow -G mailflow

WORKDIR /app

COPY --from=builder /app/target/mailflow-backend-*.jar app.jar

RUN mkdir -p /app/uploads && chown mailflow:mailflow /app/uploads

USER mailflow

EXPOSE 8080

ENV JAVA_OPTS="-Xss512k -XX:+UseContainerSupport -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0"

ENTRYPOINT ["sh", "-c", "java $JAVA_OPTS -jar app.jar"]
````

## frontend/Dockerfile

````dockerfile
# ── Stage 1: Build ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --silent

COPY . .
RUN npm run build

# ── Stage 2: Serve with nginx ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM nginx:alpine AS runtime

COPY --from=builder /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
COPY nginx.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf

EXPOSE 3000

CMD ["nginx", "-g", "daemon off;"]
````

## frontend/nginx.conf

````nginx
server {
    listen 3000;
    root /usr/share/nginx/html;
    index index.html;

    # React Router — serve index.html for all routes
    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
    }

    # Proxy API calls to backend
    location /api/ {
        proxy_pass http://backend:8080;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    }

    # Cache static assets
    location ~* \.(js|css|png|jpg|ico|svg)$ {
        expires 1y;
        add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable";
    }

    gzip on;
    gzip_types text/plain text/css application/json application/javascript;
}
````

````text
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0
                             https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>com.mailflow</groupId>
    <artifactId>mailflow-backend</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0</version>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>MailFlow</name>
    <description>Scalable Email Campaign Automation Platform</description>

    <parent>
        <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-parent</artifactId>
        <version>3.2.5</version>
        <relativePath/>
    </parent>

    <properties>
        <java.version>21</java.version>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>

        <!-- dependency versions -->
        <jjwt.version>0.12.5</jjwt.version>
        <openapi.version>2.5.0</openapi.version>
        <opencsv.version>5.9</opencsv.version>
        <apache-poi.version>5.2.5</apache-poi.version>
        <freemarker.version>2.3.32</freemarker.version>
        <testcontainers.version>1.19.8</testcontainers.version>
        <mapstruct.version>1.5.5.Final</mapstruct.version>
        <lombok.version>1.18.32</lombok.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>

        <!-- ===== Spring Boot Core ===== -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-validation</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-actuator</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-configuration-processor</artifactId>
            <optional>true</optional>
        </dependency>

        <!-- ===== Spring Data / Database ===== -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-data-jpa</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.postgresql</groupId>
            <artifactId>postgresql</artifactId>
            <scope>runtime</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.flywaydb</groupId>
            <artifactId>flyway-core</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.flywaydb</groupId>
            <artifactId>flyway-database-postgresql</artifactId>
            <version>10.15.0</version>
        </dependency>

        <!-- ===== Spring Batch ===== -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-batch</artifactId>
        </dependency>

        <!-- ===== Spring Security + JWT ===== -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-security</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.jsonwebtoken</groupId>
            <artifactId>jjwt-api</artifactId>
            <version>${jjwt.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.jsonwebtoken</groupId>
            <artifactId>jjwt-impl</artifactId>
            <version>${jjwt.version}</version>
            <scope>runtime</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.jsonwebtoken</groupId>
            <artifactId>jjwt-jackson</artifactId>
            <version>${jjwt.version}</version>
            <scope>runtime</scope>
        </dependency>

        <!-- ===== Messaging — RabbitMQ ===== -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-amqp</artifactId>
        </dependency>

        <!-- ===== Caching / Rate Limiting — Redis ===== -->

            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-data-redis</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-cache</artifactId>
        </dependency>

        <!-- ===== Email ===== -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-mail</artifactId>
        </dependency>

        <!-- ===== Template Engine (upgrade from Velocity) ===== -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.freemarker</groupId>
            <artifactId>freemarker</artifactId>
            <version>${freemarker.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-context-support</artifactId>
        </dependency>

        <!-- ===== CSV / Excel parsing ===== -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>com.opencsv</groupId>
            <artifactId>opencsv</artifactId>
            <version>${opencsv.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.apache.poi</groupId>
            <artifactId>poi-ooxml</artifactId>
            <version>${apache-poi.version}</version>
        </dependency>

        <!-- ===== OpenAPI / Swagger ===== -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springdoc</groupId>
            <artifactId>springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui</artifactId>
            <version>${openapi.version}</version>
        </dependency>

        <!-- ===== MapStruct (DTO mapping) ===== -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.mapstruct</groupId>
            <artifactId>mapstruct</artifactId>
            <version>${mapstruct.version}</version>
        </dependency>

        <!-- ===== Lombok ===== -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.projectlombok</groupId>
            <artifactId>lombok</artifactId>
            <version>${lombok.version}</version>
            <optional>true</optional>
        </dependency>

        <!-- Ensures Lombok annotation processing runs before MapStruct -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.projectlombok</groupId>
            <artifactId>lombok-mapstruct-binding</artifactId>
            <version>0.2.0</version>
        </dependency>

        <!-- ===== Scheduling — Quartz ===== -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-quartz</artifactId>
        </dependency>

        <!-- ===== HTTP Client (for AI provider) ===== -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-webflux</artifactId>
        </dependency>

        <!-- ===== Testing ===== -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.batch</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-batch-test</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.security</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-security-test</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.amqp</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-rabbit-test</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>

        <!-- Testcontainers -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.testcontainers</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <version>${testcontainers.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.testcontainers</groupId>
            <artifactId>postgresql</artifactId>
            <version>${testcontainers.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.testcontainers</groupId>
            <artifactId>rabbitmq</artifactId>
            <version>${testcontainers.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>

        <!-- H2 for lightweight unit tests (not Testcontainers) -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>com.h2database</groupId>
            <artifactId>h2</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>

    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <!-- Spring Boot plugin -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
                <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <excludes>
                        <exclude>
                            <groupId>org.projectlombok</groupId>
                            <artifactId>lombok</artifactId>
                        </exclude>
                    </excludes>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>

            <!-- Compiler: Java 21 + MapStruct + Lombok -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <release>21</release>
                    <!--
                      Lombok is on the compile classpath (see dependency below) and
                      registers itself as a JSR-269 annotation processor via
                      META-INF/services — no explicit annotationProcessorPaths needed.
                      MapStruct is NOT self-registering, so it must be listed here.
                      lombok-mapstruct-binding ensures Lombok runs before MapStruct.
                    -->
                    <annotationProcessorPaths>
                        <path>
                            <groupId>org.projectlombok</groupId>
                            <artifactId>lombok</artifactId>
                            <version>${lombok.version}</version>
                        </path>
                        <path>
                            <groupId>org.mapstruct</groupId>
                            <artifactId>mapstruct-processor</artifactId>
                            <version>${mapstruct.version}</version>
                        </path>
                        <path>
                            <groupId>org.projectlombok</groupId>
                            <artifactId>lombok-mapstruct-binding</artifactId>
                            <version>0.2.0</version>
                        </path>
                    </annotationProcessorPaths>
                    <compilerArgs>
                        <arg>-parameters</arg>
                        <arg>-Amapstruct.suppressGeneratorTimestamp=true</arg>
                        <arg>-Amapstruct.defaultComponentModel=spring</arg>
                    </compilerArgs>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>

            <!-- Surefire for test reporting -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <includes>
                        <include>**/*Test.java</include>
                        <include>**/*Tests.java</include>
                        <include>**/*IT.java</include>
                    </includes>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>

</project>
````

## render.yaml

````yaml
# Render Blueprint for the MailFlow backend (Spring Boot API + email worker).
# The frontend is deployed separately on Vercel (see frontend/vercel.json).
# Step-by-step guide: docs/DEPLOYMENT.md
#
# Values marked `sync: false` are secrets or addresses you enter in the Render
# dashboard when you create the Blueprint; they are never stored in this file.
services:
  - type: web
    name: mailflow-api
    runtime: docker
    plan: free
    dockerfilePath: ./Dockerfile
    dockerContext: .
    # Liveness only: a short outage of the database, Redis, RabbitMQ or SMTP must
    # not make Render restart the app.
    healthCheckPath: /actuator/health/liveness
    autoDeploy: true
    envVars:
      # ── App ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      - key: SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE
        value: prod
      - key: JWT_SECRET
        generateValue: true          # random 256-bit secret, created once by Render
      - key: DEMO_ACCOUNTS_ENABLED
        value: "false"
      - key: FRONTEND_URL            # e.g. https://mailflow.vercel.app (comma-separate several)
        sync: false
      - key: APP_BASE_URL            # this service's URL, e.g. https://mailflow-api.onrender.com
        sync: false
      # The free instance has 512 MB: keep the heap well below it.
      - key: JAVA_OPTS
        value: "-Xss512k -XX:+UseContainerSupport -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=60.0 -XX:+UseSerialGC"

      # ── PostgreSQL (Neon) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
      - key: DB_URL                  # jdbc:postgresql://<host>/<db>?sslmode=require
        sync: false
      - key: DB_USERNAME
        sync: false
      - key: DB_PASSWORD
        sync: false
      - key: DB_POOL_SIZE
        value: "5"

      # ── Redis (Upstash) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      - key: REDIS_HOST
        sync: false
      - key: REDIS_PORT
        value: "6379"
      - key: REDIS_PASSWORD
        sync: false
      - key: REDIS_SSL
        value: "true"

      # ── RabbitMQ (CloudAMQP) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
      - key: RABBITMQ_HOST
        sync: false
      - key: RABBITMQ_PORT
        value: "5671"
      - key: RABBITMQ_SSL
        value: "true"
      - key: RABBITMQ_USERNAME
        sync: false
      - key: RABBITMQ_PASSWORD
        sync: false
      - key: RABBITMQ_VHOST          # on CloudAMQP, the same as the user name
        sync: false

      # ── Email (Brevo SMTP) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
      - key: EMAIL_MODE
        value: production
      - key: SMTP_HOST
        value: smtp-relay.brevo.com
      # Brevo also listens on 2525. Render's free plan blocks outgoing SMTP on 25, 465
      # and 587 (the connection times out), so 2525 is used; STARTTLS still applies.
      - key: SMTP_PORT
        value: "2525"
      - key: SMTP_AUTH
        value: "true"
      - key: SMTP_TLS
        value: "true"
      - key: SMTP_USERNAME           # Brevo SMTP login, e.g. 1234abc@smtp-brevo.com
        sync: false
      - key: SMTP_PASSWORD           # Brevo SMTP key (not your Brevo account password)
        sync: false
      - key: EMAIL_FROM_POLICY       # From = EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS; each campaign's sender becomes Reply-To
        value: platform
      - key: EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS      # a sender address verified in Brevo
        sync: false
      - key: EMAIL_FROM_NAME
        value: MailFlow
      - key: EMAIL_RATE_LIMIT        # per minute; Brevo's free plan allows 300 emails a day
        value: "20"
````

## src/main/resources/application.yml

````yaml
spring:
  application:
    name: mailflow

  # ── Database ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  datasource:
    url: ${DB_URL:jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/mailflow}
    username: ${DB_USERNAME:mailflow}
    password: ${DB_PASSWORD:mailflow}
    driver-class-name: org.postgresql.Driver
    hikari:
      pool-name: MailFlowPool
      # Hosted free databases (Neon) allow few connections: set DB_POOL_SIZE=5 there.
      maximum-pool-size: ${DB_POOL_SIZE:20}
      minimum-idle: ${DB_POOL_MIN_IDLE:2}
      connection-timeout: 30000
      idle-timeout: 600000
      max-lifetime: 1800000

  # ── JPA / Hibernate ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  jpa:
    # Company isolation relies on this: the request's Hibernate session is opened after
    # the security filter signs the user in, so it is filtered to their organization.
    open-in-view: true
    hibernate:
      ddl-auto: validate          # Flyway owns schema creation
    show-sql: false
    properties:
      hibernate:
        dialect: org.hibernate.dialect.PostgreSQLDialect
        format_sql: true
        default_batch_fetch_size: 50
        jdbc:
          batch_size: 50
        order_inserts: true
        order_updates: true
        # Fills and filters each entity's @TenantId (organization) from the signed-in user.
        tenant_identifier_resolver: com.mailflow.tenant.TenantIdentifierResolver

  # ── Flyway ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flyway:
    enabled: true
    locations: classpath:db/migration
    baseline-on-migrate: false
    validate-on-migrate: true

  # ── Spring Batch ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  batch:
    job:
      enabled: false              # Jobs are triggered programmatically, not on startup
    jdbc:
      initialize-schema: never    # Flyway handles batch schema too

  # ── RabbitMQ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  rabbitmq:
    host: ${RABBITMQ_HOST:localhost}
    port: ${RABBITMQ_PORT:5672}
    username: ${RABBITMQ_USERNAME:guest}
    password: ${RABBITMQ_PASSWORD:guest}
    # CloudAMQP: the virtual host is your instance's user name; set RABBITMQ_SSL=true with port 5671.
    virtual-host: ${RABBITMQ_VHOST:/}
    # connection-timeout=0 means wait indefinitely but lazy=true means
    # the connection is only established when first needed, not on startup.
    # This allows the app to start even when RabbitMQ is temporarily unavailable.
    connection-timeout: 5000
    listener:
      simple:
        prefetch: 10
        auto-startup: true
        retry:
          enabled: true
          initial-interval: 2000
          max-attempts: 3
          multiplier: 2.0
          max-interval: 10000
    template:
      retry:
        enabled: true
        initial-interval: 1000
        max-attempts: 3
        multiplier: 1.5

  # ── Redis ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  data:
    redis:
      host: ${REDIS_HOST:localhost}
      port: ${REDIS_PORT:6379}
      password: ${REDIS_PASSWORD:}
      # Upstash and most hosted Redis require TLS: REDIS_SSL=true
      ssl:
        enabled: ${REDIS_SSL:false}
      timeout: 5000
      lettuce:
        pool:
          max-active: 16
          max-idle: 8
          min-idle: 2

  # ── Mail (SMTP) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Fully environment-driven. Two tested configurations:
  #
  #   MailHog (local dev — default):
  #     SMTP_HOST=localhost  SMTP_PORT=1025  SMTP_AUTH=false  SMTP_TLS=false
  #
  #   Gmail SMTP (real delivery):
  #     SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com  SMTP_PORT=587  SMTP_AUTH=true  SMTP_TLS=true
  #     SMTP_USERNAME=<gmail-address>  SMTP_PASSWORD=<google-app-password>
  #
  # NEVER commit real credentials. See docs/EMAIL_SMTP_SETUP.md.
  mail:
    host: ${SMTP_HOST:localhost}
    port: ${SMTP_PORT:1025}
    username: ${SMTP_USERNAME:}
    password: ${SMTP_PASSWORD:}
    properties:
      mail:
        smtp:
          auth: ${SMTP_AUTH:false}
          starttls:
            # enable negotiates STARTTLS if the server offers it;
            # required (tied to the same SMTP_TLS flag) refuses to send
            # over an un-encrypted channel — mandatory for Gmail on 587.
            enable: ${SMTP_TLS:false}
            required: ${SMTP_TLS:false}
          # mail.smtp.ssl.trust is set only when SMTP_SSL_TRUST has a value (see
          # SmtpSslTrustConfig): an empty value would make Jakarta Mail trust no server.
          # Timeouts (ms). Gmail can be slower than a local MailHog, so the
          # defaults are generous but overridable per environment.
          connectiontimeout: ${SMTP_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS:10000}
          timeout: ${SMTP_READ_TIMEOUT_MS:10000}
          writetimeout: ${SMTP_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS:10000}
    test-connection: false

  # ── Servlet / File Upload ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  servlet:
    multipart:
      max-file-size: 25MB
      max-request-size: 30MB

  # ── FreeMarker (email templates) ──────────────────────────────────────────
  freemarker:
    enabled: false  # We configure it manually (not for MVC views)

  # ── Cache ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  cache:
    type: redis
    redis:
      time-to-live: 600000  # 10 minutes default

# ── Server ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
server:
  # Render and similar hosts tell the app which port to use through PORT.
  port: ${PORT:${SERVER_PORT:8080}}
  error:
    include-message: always
    include-binding-errors: always
    include-stacktrace: never
    include-exception: false

# ── Actuator ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health,info,metrics,prometheus,loggers
      base-path: /actuator
  endpoint:
    health:
      # /actuator/health/liveness answers UP while the app runs, whatever the state of the
      # database, Redis, RabbitMQ or SMTP: the host's health check uses it, so a short
      # outage of one of those does not get the app restarted.
      probes:
        enabled: true
      show-details: when_authorized
      show-components: when_authorized
  info:
    env:
      enabled: true

# ── OpenAPI / Swagger ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
springdoc:
  api-docs:
    path: /v3/api-docs
  swagger-ui:
    path: /swagger-ui.html
    operationsSorter: method
    tagsSorter: alpha
  show-actuator: false

# ── JWT ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
mailflow:
  security:
    jwt:
      secret: ${JWT_SECRET:change-me-in-production-must-be-at-least-256-bits-long-secret-key}
      access-token-expiry-ms: ${JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRY_MS:3600000}      # 1 hour
      refresh-token-expiry-ms: ${JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRY_MS:604800000}  # 7 days
    # Seeded demo accounts with published passwords. false on any public deployment.
    demo-accounts-enabled: ${DEMO_ACCOUNTS_ENABLED:true}

  # ── Email Engine ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  email:
    from-name: ${EMAIL_FROM_NAME:MailFlow Platform}
    from-address: ${EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS:noreply@mailflow.local}
    rate-limit-per-minute: ${EMAIL_RATE_LIMIT:100}
    mode: ${EMAIL_MODE:development}   # development | production
    from-policy: ${EMAIL_FROM_POLICY:smtp-username}   # smtp-username (Gmail) | platform (Brevo, SES)

  # ── Batch ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  batch:
    chunk-size: ${BATCH_CHUNK_SIZE:50}
    max-retries: ${BATCH_MAX_RETRIES:3}
    skip-limit: ${BATCH_SKIP_LIMIT:100}
    throttle-limit: ${BATCH_THROTTLE_LIMIT:4}

  # ── File Storage ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  storage:
    upload-dir: ${UPLOAD_DIR:./uploads}
    max-attachment-size-mb: ${MAX_ATTACHMENT_MB:10}
    allowed-mime-types: >
      application/pdf,
      application/msword,
      application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document,
      image/png,image/jpeg,image/gif,
      text/plain,
      application/zip

  # ── AI Email Copilot ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ai:
    enabled: ${AI_ENABLED:false}
    provider: ${AI_PROVIDER:gemini}   # gemini | openai
    openai:
      api-key: ${OPENAI_API_KEY:}
      model: ${OPENAI_MODEL:gpt-4o-mini}
      base-url: https://api.openai.com/v1
      timeout-seconds: 30
    gemini:
      api-key: ${GEMINI_API_KEY:}
      model: ${GEMINI_MODEL:gemini-1.5-flash}
      base-url: ${GEMINI_BASE_URL:https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta}
      timeout-seconds: ${GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:30}

  # ── Unsubscribe ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  unsubscribe:
    base-url: ${APP_BASE_URL:http://localhost:8080}
    token-expiry-days: 365

# ── Logging ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
logging:
  level:
    root: INFO
    com.mailflow: DEBUG
    org.springframework.batch: INFO
    org.springframework.security: INFO
    org.hibernate.SQL: WARN
    org.flywaydb: INFO
  pattern:
    console: "%d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS} [%thread] %-5level %logger{36} - %msg%n"
````

## src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__init_schema.sql

````sql
-- =============================================================================
-- V1 — MailFlow initial schema
-- =============================================================================
-- Conventions:
--   • All PKs are BIGSERIAL (auto-increment).
--   • Timestamps stored as TIMESTAMPTZ (UTC).
--   • Soft-delete patterns use deleted_at rather than a boolean flag.
--   • JSON columns used for extensible custom fields only.
-- =============================================================================

-- ─── Extensions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "pgcrypto";

-- =============================================================================
-- USERS & ROLES
-- =============================================================================

CREATE TABLE roles (
    id          BIGSERIAL       PRIMARY KEY,
    name        VARCHAR(50)     NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    description VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE users (
    id              BIGSERIAL       PRIMARY KEY,
    email           VARCHAR(255)    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    password_hash   VARCHAR(255)    NOT NULL,
    first_name      VARCHAR(100)    NOT NULL,
    last_name       VARCHAR(100)    NOT NULL,
    enabled         BOOLEAN         NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    deleted_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
    version         BIGINT          NOT NULL DEFAULT 0   -- optimistic locking
);

CREATE TABLE user_roles (
    user_id     BIGINT  NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    role_id     BIGINT  NOT NULL REFERENCES roles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, role_id)
);

-- =============================================================================
-- RECIPIENTS
-- =============================================================================

CREATE TABLE recipient_groups (
    id          BIGSERIAL       PRIMARY KEY,
    name        VARCHAR(255)    NOT NULL,
    description TEXT,
    created_by  BIGINT          REFERENCES users(id),
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE recipients (
    id              BIGSERIAL       PRIMARY KEY,
    email           VARCHAR(255)    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    name            VARCHAR(255),
    first_name      VARCHAR(100),
    last_name       VARCHAR(100),
    company         VARCHAR(255),
    course          VARCHAR(255),
    custom_fields   JSONB           NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    status          VARCHAR(50)     NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ACTIVE',  -- ACTIVE | UNSUBSCRIBED | BOUNCED | INVALID
    import_source   VARCHAR(100),                               -- 'CSV_UPLOAD' | 'API' | 'MANUAL'
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    deleted_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
    version         BIGINT          NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE TABLE recipient_group_members (
    recipient_id    BIGINT  NOT NULL REFERENCES recipients(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    group_id        BIGINT  NOT NULL REFERENCES recipient_groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    added_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    PRIMARY KEY (recipient_id, group_id)
);

-- =============================================================================
-- UNSUBSCRIBE
-- =============================================================================

CREATE TABLE unsubscribe_list (
    id              BIGSERIAL       PRIMARY KEY,
    email           VARCHAR(255)    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    token           VARCHAR(64)     NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    reason          TEXT,
    unsubscribed_at TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    campaign_id     BIGINT          -- FK added after campaigns table
);

-- =============================================================================
-- EMAIL TEMPLATES
-- =============================================================================

CREATE TABLE email_templates (
    id              BIGSERIAL       PRIMARY KEY,
    name            VARCHAR(255)    NOT NULL,
    description     TEXT,
    subject         TEXT            NOT NULL,
    html_body       TEXT,
    plain_body      TEXT,
    variables       JSONB           NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',  -- ["name","email","course"]
    created_by      BIGINT          REFERENCES users(id),
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    deleted_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
    version         BIGINT          NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

-- =============================================================================
-- ATTACHMENTS
-- =============================================================================

CREATE TABLE attachments (
    id              BIGSERIAL       PRIMARY KEY,
    original_name   VARCHAR(500)    NOT NULL,
    stored_name     VARCHAR(500)    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    content_type    VARCHAR(255)    NOT NULL,
    size_bytes      BIGINT          NOT NULL,
    storage_path    TEXT            NOT NULL,
    uploaded_by     BIGINT          REFERENCES users(id),
    uploaded_at     TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- =============================================================================
-- CAMPAIGNS
-- =============================================================================

CREATE TABLE campaigns (
    id                  BIGSERIAL       PRIMARY KEY,
    name                VARCHAR(255)    NOT NULL,
    description         TEXT,
    subject             TEXT            NOT NULL,
    template_id         BIGINT          REFERENCES email_templates(id),
    sender_name         VARCHAR(255),
    sender_email        VARCHAR(255),
    reply_to            VARCHAR(255),
    status              VARCHAR(50)     NOT NULL DEFAULT 'DRAFT',
    -- DRAFT | SCHEDULED | QUEUED | RUNNING | PAUSED | COMPLETED | FAILED | CANCELLED
    scheduled_at        TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_by          BIGINT          REFERENCES users(id),
    created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at          TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    started_at          TIMESTAMPTZ,
    completed_at        TIMESTAMPTZ,
    total_recipients    BIGINT          NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    sent_count          BIGINT          NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    failed_count        BIGINT          NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    skipped_count       BIGINT          NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    bounced_count       BIGINT          NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    retry_count         BIGINT          NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    batch_job_id        VARCHAR(255),   -- Spring Batch job execution ID reference
    version             BIGINT          NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

-- =============================================================================
-- CAMPAIGN RECIPIENTS (join table with per-recipient delivery state)
-- =============================================================================

CREATE TABLE campaign_recipients (
    id                  BIGSERIAL       PRIMARY KEY,
    campaign_id         BIGINT          NOT NULL REFERENCES campaigns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    recipient_id        BIGINT          NOT NULL REFERENCES recipients(id),
    delivery_status     VARCHAR(50)     NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PENDING',
    -- PENDING | QUEUED | SENT | FAILED | SKIPPED | BOUNCED
    idempotency_key     VARCHAR(100)    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    -- Prevents duplicate sends: format = campaign_{id}_recipient_{id}
    queued_at           TIMESTAMPTZ,
    sent_at             TIMESTAMPTZ,
    failed_at           TIMESTAMPTZ,
    retry_count         INT             NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    last_error          TEXT,
    personalized_subject TEXT,
    UNIQUE (campaign_id, recipient_id)
);

-- =============================================================================
-- EMAIL LOGS (detailed per-message audit trail)
-- =============================================================================

CREATE TABLE email_logs (
    id                  BIGSERIAL       PRIMARY KEY,
    campaign_id         BIGINT          NOT NULL REFERENCES campaigns(id),
    recipient_id        BIGINT          REFERENCES recipients(id),
    campaign_recipient_id BIGINT        REFERENCES campaign_recipients(id),
    to_address          VARCHAR(255)    NOT NULL,
    subject             TEXT,
    status              VARCHAR(50)     NOT NULL,
    -- SENT | FAILED | RETRYING | SKIPPED
    provider_message_id VARCHAR(500),   -- ID returned by SMTP/provider
    error_message       TEXT,
    error_type          VARCHAR(100),   -- TEMPORARY | PERMANENT
    attempt_number      INT             NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    processed_at        TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- =============================================================================
-- EMAIL EVENTS (open/click tracking)
-- =============================================================================

CREATE TABLE email_events (
    id              BIGSERIAL       PRIMARY KEY,
    email_log_id    BIGINT          REFERENCES email_logs(id),
    campaign_id     BIGINT          REFERENCES campaigns(id),
    recipient_id    BIGINT          REFERENCES recipients(id),
    event_type      VARCHAR(50)     NOT NULL,  -- OPENED | CLICKED | BOUNCED | COMPLAINED
    event_data      JSONB,
    user_agent      TEXT,
    ip_address      VARCHAR(45),
    occurred_at     TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- =============================================================================
-- SCHEDULED CAMPAIGNS
-- =============================================================================

CREATE TABLE scheduled_campaigns (
    id              BIGSERIAL       PRIMARY KEY,
    campaign_id     BIGINT          NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES campaigns(id),
    scheduled_at    TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL,
    timezone        VARCHAR(100)    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UTC',
    quartz_job_key  VARCHAR(255),
    status          VARCHAR(50)     NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PENDING',
    -- PENDING | TRIGGERED | CANCELLED
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    triggered_at    TIMESTAMPTZ
);

-- =============================================================================
-- DELAYED: add FK from unsubscribe_list to campaigns
-- =============================================================================
ALTER TABLE unsubscribe_list
    ADD CONSTRAINT fk_unsubscribe_campaign
    FOREIGN KEY (campaign_id) REFERENCES campaigns(id);

-- =============================================================================
-- INDEXES
-- =============================================================================

-- Users
CREATE INDEX idx_users_email         ON users(email);
CREATE INDEX idx_users_enabled       ON users(enabled) WHERE enabled = TRUE;

-- Recipients
CREATE INDEX idx_recipients_email    ON recipients(email);
CREATE INDEX idx_recipients_status   ON recipients(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_recipients_deleted  ON recipients(deleted_at) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;

-- Campaigns
CREATE INDEX idx_campaigns_status       ON campaigns(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_campaigns_created_by   ON campaigns(created_by);
CREATE INDEX idx_campaigns_scheduled_at ON campaigns(scheduled_at) WHERE scheduled_at IS NOT NULL;

-- Campaign recipients
CREATE INDEX idx_cr_campaign    ON campaign_recipients(campaign_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_cr_recipient   ON campaign_recipients(recipient_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_cr_status      ON campaign_recipients(delivery_status);
CREATE INDEX idx_cr_idem_key    ON campaign_recipients(idempotency_key);

-- Email logs
CREATE INDEX idx_email_logs_campaign    ON email_logs(campaign_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_email_logs_recipient   ON email_logs(recipient_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_email_logs_status      ON email_logs(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_email_logs_processed   ON email_logs(processed_at);

-- Email events
CREATE INDEX idx_email_events_campaign  ON email_events(campaign_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_email_events_type      ON email_events(event_type);

-- Unsubscribe
CREATE INDEX idx_unsub_email    ON unsubscribe_list(email);
CREATE INDEX idx_unsub_token    ON unsubscribe_list(token);

-- Templates
CREATE INDEX idx_templates_deleted ON email_templates(deleted_at) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
````

## src/main/resources/db/migration/V2__spring_batch_schema.sql

````sql
-- =============================================================================
-- V2 — Spring Batch metadata tables (PostgreSQL dialect)
-- =============================================================================
-- Copied from Spring Batch's schema-postgresql.sql and adjusted for our
-- Flyway-managed schema. Spring is configured with jdbc.initialize-schema=never
-- so we own this DDL.
-- =============================================================================

CREATE TABLE BATCH_JOB_INSTANCE (
    JOB_INSTANCE_ID BIGINT       NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    VERSION         BIGINT,
    JOB_NAME        VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    JOB_KEY         VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT JOB_INST_UN UNIQUE (JOB_NAME, JOB_KEY)
);

CREATE TABLE BATCH_JOB_EXECUTION (
    JOB_EXECUTION_ID    BIGINT          NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    VERSION             BIGINT,
    JOB_INSTANCE_ID     BIGINT          NOT NULL,
    CREATE_TIME         TIMESTAMP       NOT NULL,
    START_TIME          TIMESTAMP       DEFAULT NULL,
    END_TIME            TIMESTAMP       DEFAULT NULL,
    STATUS              VARCHAR(10),
    EXIT_CODE           VARCHAR(2500),
    EXIT_MESSAGE        VARCHAR(2500),
    LAST_UPDATED        TIMESTAMP,
    CONSTRAINT JOB_INST_EXEC_FK FOREIGN KEY (JOB_INSTANCE_ID)
        REFERENCES BATCH_JOB_INSTANCE(JOB_INSTANCE_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE BATCH_JOB_EXECUTION_PARAMS (
    JOB_EXECUTION_ID BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    PARAMETER_NAME   VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    PARAMETER_TYPE   VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    PARAMETER_VALUE  VARCHAR(2500),
    IDENTIFYING      CHAR(1)      NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT JOB_EXEC_PARAMS_FK FOREIGN KEY (JOB_EXECUTION_ID)
        REFERENCES BATCH_JOB_EXECUTION(JOB_EXECUTION_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE BATCH_STEP_EXECUTION (
    STEP_EXECUTION_ID   BIGINT          NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    VERSION             BIGINT          NOT NULL,
    STEP_NAME           VARCHAR(100)    NOT NULL,
    JOB_EXECUTION_ID    BIGINT          NOT NULL,
    CREATE_TIME         TIMESTAMP       NOT NULL,
    START_TIME          TIMESTAMP       DEFAULT NULL,
    END_TIME            TIMESTAMP       DEFAULT NULL,
    STATUS              VARCHAR(10),
    COMMIT_COUNT        BIGINT,
    READ_COUNT          BIGINT,
    FILTER_COUNT        BIGINT,
    WRITE_COUNT         BIGINT,
    READ_SKIP_COUNT     BIGINT,
    WRITE_SKIP_COUNT    BIGINT,
    PROCESS_SKIP_COUNT  BIGINT,
    ROLLBACK_COUNT      BIGINT,
    EXIT_CODE           VARCHAR(2500),
    EXIT_MESSAGE        VARCHAR(2500),
    LAST_UPDATED        TIMESTAMP,
    CONSTRAINT JOB_EXEC_STEP_FK FOREIGN KEY (JOB_EXECUTION_ID)
        REFERENCES BATCH_JOB_EXECUTION(JOB_EXECUTION_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE BATCH_STEP_EXECUTION_CONTEXT (
    STEP_EXECUTION_ID   BIGINT          NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    SHORT_CONTEXT       VARCHAR(2500)   NOT NULL,
    SERIALIZED_CONTEXT  TEXT,
    CONSTRAINT STEP_EXEC_CTX_FK FOREIGN KEY (STEP_EXECUTION_ID)
        REFERENCES BATCH_STEP_EXECUTION(STEP_EXECUTION_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE BATCH_JOB_EXECUTION_CONTEXT (
    JOB_EXECUTION_ID    BIGINT          NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    SHORT_CONTEXT       VARCHAR(2500)   NOT NULL,
    SERIALIZED_CONTEXT  TEXT,
    CONSTRAINT JOB_EXEC_CTX_FK FOREIGN KEY (JOB_EXECUTION_ID)
        REFERENCES BATCH_JOB_EXECUTION(JOB_EXECUTION_ID)
);

-- Sequences for Spring Batch
CREATE SEQUENCE BATCH_STEP_EXECUTION_SEQ MAXVALUE 9223372036854775807 NO CYCLE;
CREATE SEQUENCE BATCH_JOB_EXECUTION_SEQ  MAXVALUE 9223372036854775807 NO CYCLE;
CREATE SEQUENCE BATCH_JOB_SEQ            MAXVALUE 9223372036854775807 NO CYCLE;
````

## src/main/resources/db/migration/V3__seed_data.sql

````sql
-- =============================================================================
-- V3 — Seed data for local development / demo
-- =============================================================================
-- IMPORTANT: These are DEMO credentials. Change them before any real deployment.
--
-- Admin:            admin@mailflow.local       / Admin@123
-- Campaign Manager: manager@mailflow.local     / Manager@123
-- Viewer:           viewer@mailflow.local      / Viewer@123
--
-- Passwords are BCrypt-hashed (cost 12).
-- =============================================================================

-- Roles
INSERT INTO roles (name, description) VALUES
    ('ADMIN',            'Full system access'),
    ('CAMPAIGN_MANAGER', 'Create and manage campaigns, recipients, templates'),
    ('VIEWER',           'Read-only analytics and reporting')
ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING;

-- Users (BCrypt hash of Admin@123, Manager@123, Viewer@123)
INSERT INTO users (email, password_hash, first_name, last_name, enabled) VALUES
    ('admin@mailflow.local',
     '$2a$12$QAs4bs8wloGrgZh0d0Tc0ud9E6OeQij.KmbcIi8fmHtUpUGs9fd0a',
     'Admin', 'User', TRUE),
    ('manager@mailflow.local',
     '$2a$12$08kG7KkUDvuh1jLJqY7DOueqKxa3Ic86v7SIymxRWcV3XyLmNVlUC',
     'Campaign', 'Manager', TRUE),
    ('viewer@mailflow.local',
     '$2a$12$5wz6U1uNpE65GXP/NWL2z.QtJHdMukvTUJNHUHCt9TPVOVckiSU9W',
     'Analytics', 'Viewer', TRUE)
ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING;

-- User-Role assignments
INSERT INTO user_roles (user_id, role_id)
SELECT u.id, r.id FROM users u CROSS JOIN roles r
WHERE u.email = 'admin@mailflow.local'
  AND r.name IN ('ADMIN', 'CAMPAIGN_MANAGER', 'VIEWER')
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

INSERT INTO user_roles (user_id, role_id)
SELECT u.id, r.id FROM users u CROSS JOIN roles r
WHERE u.email = 'manager@mailflow.local'
  AND r.name IN ('CAMPAIGN_MANAGER', 'VIEWER')
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

INSERT INTO user_roles (user_id, role_id)
SELECT u.id, r.id FROM users u CROSS JOIN roles r
WHERE u.email = 'viewer@mailflow.local'
  AND r.name = 'VIEWER'
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

-- Recipient Groups ("descr" alias — "desc" is a reserved keyword in PostgreSQL)
INSERT INTO recipient_groups (name, description, created_by)
SELECT
    grp.name,
    grp.descr,
    (SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = 'admin@mailflow.local')
FROM (VALUES
    ('CS Final Year 2026',   'Computer Science graduates 2026'),
    ('IT Department',        'Information Technology batch'),
    ('MBA Cohort 2026',      'MBA students graduation batch')
) AS grp(name, descr);

-- Email Templates
INSERT INTO email_templates (name, description, subject, html_body, plain_body, variables, created_by)
SELECT
    'Placement Workshop Invitation',
    'Invite students to campus placement workshop',
    'Invitation: Placement Preparation Workshop — {{name}}',
    '<html><body><p>Dear <strong>{{name}}</strong>,</p><p>We are pleased to invite you to the <strong>Placement Preparation Workshop</strong> on October 15, 2026.</p><p>Course: {{course}} | Code: <code>{{code}}</code></p><p>Register at: https://placement.example.com</p><p>Best regards,<br/>Placement Cell</p></body></html>',
    'Dear {{name}}, You are invited to the Placement Preparation Workshop on October 15, 2026. Course: {{course}} | Code: {{code}}. Register at: https://placement.example.com',
    '["name","email","course","company","code"]'::jsonb,
    (SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = 'admin@mailflow.local')
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM email_templates WHERE name = 'Placement Workshop Invitation');

INSERT INTO email_templates (name, description, subject, html_body, plain_body, variables, created_by)
SELECT
    'Cloud Lab Access',
    'Send cloud lab registration codes to students',
    'Your Cloud Lab Access Code — {{name}}',
    '<html><body><p>Hi <strong>{{name}}</strong>,</p><p>Your access code for the <strong>{{course}}</strong> cloud lab is: <code>{{code}}</code></p><p>Visit https://labs.example.com to redeem.</p><p>— MailFlow Team</p></body></html>',
    'Hi {{name}}, Your code for {{course}}: {{code}}. Visit https://labs.example.com. — MailFlow Team',
    '["name","email","course","code"]'::jsonb,
    (SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = 'admin@mailflow.local')
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM email_templates WHERE name = 'Cloud Lab Access');

-- Demo Recipients (100 records)
INSERT INTO recipients (email, name, first_name, last_name, course, company, custom_fields, import_source, status)
SELECT
    'student' || n || '@demo.mailflow.local',
    'Student ' || n,
    'Student',
    n::TEXT,
    CASE WHEN n % 3 = 0 THEN 'Computer Science'
         WHEN n % 3 = 1 THEN 'Information Technology'
         ELSE 'MBA' END,
    CASE WHEN n % 4 = 0 THEN 'TechCorp'
         WHEN n % 4 = 1 THEN 'InnoSoft'
         WHEN n % 4 = 2 THEN 'DataSystems'
         ELSE 'CloudBase' END,
    ('{"code": "CODE-' || LPAD(n::TEXT, 4, '0') || '"}')::jsonb,
    'SEED_DATA',
    'ACTIVE'
FROM generate_series(1, 100) AS n
ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING;

-- Sample DRAFT Campaign
INSERT INTO campaigns (name, description, subject, template_id, status, created_by,
                       sender_name, sender_email, total_recipients)
SELECT
    'Placement Workshop 2026',
    'Campus placement preparation workshop invitation campaign',
    'Invitation: Placement Preparation Workshop',
    (SELECT id FROM email_templates WHERE name = 'Placement Workshop Invitation' LIMIT 1),
    'DRAFT',
    (SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = 'admin@mailflow.local'),
    'Placement Cell',
    'placement@mailflow.local',
    100
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM campaigns WHERE name = 'Placement Workshop 2026');
````

````sql
-- =============================================================================
-- V4 — Campaign target groups and recipients join tables
-- =============================================================================

CREATE TABLE campaign_target_groups (
    campaign_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES campaigns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    group_id    BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES recipient_groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    PRIMARY KEY (campaign_id, group_id)
);

CREATE TABLE campaign_target_recipients (
    campaign_id  BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES campaigns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    recipient_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES recipients(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    PRIMARY KEY (campaign_id, recipient_id)
);

CREATE TABLE campaign_attachments (
    campaign_id   BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES campaigns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    attachment_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES attachments(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    PRIMARY KEY (campaign_id, attachment_id)
);
````

## src/main/resources/db/migration/V5__campaign_only_addresses.sql

````sql
-- =============================================================================
-- V5 — Campaign-only addresses
-- =============================================================================
-- Lets a campaign email typed or uploaded addresses WITHOUT creating saved
-- contacts. Additive only: no existing row, column or constraint is removed,
-- and existing data keeps its meaning.
--
--   • campaign_target_addresses holds a campaign's campaign-only addresses
--     (what a draft will send to). Rows are deleted with the campaign.
--   • campaign_recipients.recipient_id becomes nullable. A row without a
--     recipient delivers to a campaign-only address and carries a snapshot of
--     it (email, name, first_name, last_name, company, custom_fields).
--     Existing rows keep their recipient_id; their snapshot columns stay NULL.
-- =============================================================================

CREATE TABLE campaign_target_addresses (
    id              BIGSERIAL       PRIMARY KEY,
    campaign_id     BIGINT          NOT NULL REFERENCES campaigns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    email           VARCHAR(255)    NOT NULL,   -- stored lower-case
    name            VARCHAR(255),
    first_name      VARCHAR(100),
    last_name       VARCHAR(100),
    company         VARCHAR(255),
    custom_fields   JSONB           NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    CONSTRAINT uq_campaign_target_addresses_email UNIQUE (campaign_id, email),
    CONSTRAINT ck_campaign_target_addresses_lower CHECK (email = lower(email))
);

-- A campaign-only delivery row has no saved contact ...
ALTER TABLE campaign_recipients ALTER COLUMN recipient_id DROP NOT NULL;

-- ... and carries a snapshot of the address instead (NULL on saved-contact rows).
ALTER TABLE campaign_recipients
    ADD COLUMN email            VARCHAR(255),
    ADD COLUMN name             VARCHAR(255),
    ADD COLUMN first_name       VARCHAR(100),
    ADD COLUMN last_name        VARCHAR(100),
    ADD COLUMN company          VARCHAR(255),
    ADD COLUMN custom_fields    JSONB;

-- Every delivery row must say where it sends to.
ALTER TABLE campaign_recipients
    ADD CONSTRAINT ck_campaign_recipients_target
    CHECK (recipient_id IS NOT NULL OR email IS NOT NULL);

-- At most one campaign-only row per address in a campaign.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_campaign_recipients_address
    ON campaign_recipients (campaign_id, lower(email))
    WHERE recipient_id IS NULL;
````

## src/main/resources/db/migration/V6__campaign_soft_delete.sql

````sql
-- =============================================================================
-- V6 — Campaign soft delete
-- =============================================================================
-- Deleting a campaign hides it instead of removing its row. email_logs (the
-- per-message audit trail), email_events, unsubscribe_list and
-- scheduled_campaigns reference campaigns without ON DELETE CASCADE, and the
-- delivery history and unsubscribe entries must be kept, so the row stays.
--
-- Additive only: two nullable columns and an index. Existing campaigns keep
-- deleted_at NULL, which means "not deleted"; no existing row is changed.
--
--   • deleted_at: when the campaign was deleted (NULL for a live campaign).
--   • deleted_by: the user who deleted it (NULL when not known).
-- =============================================================================

ALTER TABLE campaigns
    ADD COLUMN deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    ADD COLUMN deleted_by BIGINT REFERENCES users(id);

-- Same convention as recipients and email_templates: lists read live rows only.
CREATE INDEX idx_campaigns_deleted ON campaigns(deleted_at) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
````

## src/main/resources/db/migration/V7__campaign_custom_body.sql

````sql
-- =============================================================================
-- V7 — Campaign-wide email body
-- =============================================================================
-- A campaign can carry its own plain-text email body, written in the New
-- Campaign form, instead of a template's body. The subject stays in
-- campaigns.subject.
--
-- Additive only: one nullable column. NULL means "use the template's body",
-- which is what every existing campaign does today, so no existing row changes.
--
--   • custom_body: the campaign's own body (plain text, placeholders such as
--     {{FirstName}} allowed). When set, it is sent instead of the template's
--     bodies. The API limits it to 100,000 characters.
-- =============================================================================

ALTER TABLE campaigns ADD COLUMN custom_body TEXT;
````

## src/main/resources/db/migration/V8__organizations.sql

````sql
-- =============================================================================
-- V8 — Organizations (company workspaces)
-- =============================================================================
-- Every user belongs to one organization, and every recipient, group, template,
-- campaign, attachment and unsubscribe entry is owned by one. Existing rows are
-- moved into a "Default" organization, so an existing install keeps working.
--
-- Email addresses become unique per organization: two companies may each have
-- the same contact, and an opt-out applies to the company it was made for.
-- =============================================================================

CREATE TABLE organizations (
    id          BIGSERIAL       PRIMARY KEY,
    name        VARCHAR(255)    NOT NULL,
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

INSERT INTO organizations (name) VALUES ('Default');

-- ── Users ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN organization_id BIGINT REFERENCES organizations(id);
UPDATE users SET organization_id = (SELECT MIN(id) FROM organizations);
ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN organization_id SET NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_users_org ON users(organization_id);

-- ── Company-owned data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ALTER TABLE recipients        ADD COLUMN organization_id BIGINT REFERENCES organizations(id);
ALTER TABLE recipient_groups  ADD COLUMN organization_id BIGINT REFERENCES organizations(id);
ALTER TABLE email_templates   ADD COLUMN organization_id BIGINT REFERENCES organizations(id);
ALTER TABLE attachments       ADD COLUMN organization_id BIGINT REFERENCES organizations(id);
ALTER TABLE campaigns         ADD COLUMN organization_id BIGINT REFERENCES organizations(id);
ALTER TABLE unsubscribe_list  ADD COLUMN organization_id BIGINT REFERENCES organizations(id);

UPDATE recipients       SET organization_id = (SELECT MIN(id) FROM organizations);
UPDATE recipient_groups SET organization_id = (SELECT MIN(id) FROM organizations);
UPDATE email_templates  SET organization_id = (SELECT MIN(id) FROM organizations);
UPDATE attachments      SET organization_id = (SELECT MIN(id) FROM organizations);
UPDATE campaigns        SET organization_id = (SELECT MIN(id) FROM organizations);
UPDATE unsubscribe_list SET organization_id = (SELECT MIN(id) FROM organizations);

ALTER TABLE recipients       ALTER COLUMN organization_id SET NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE recipient_groups ALTER COLUMN organization_id SET NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE email_templates  ALTER COLUMN organization_id SET NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE attachments      ALTER COLUMN organization_id SET NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE campaigns        ALTER COLUMN organization_id SET NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE unsubscribe_list ALTER COLUMN organization_id SET NOT NULL;

CREATE INDEX idx_recipients_org       ON recipients(organization_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_recipient_groups_org ON recipient_groups(organization_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_email_templates_org  ON email_templates(organization_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_attachments_org      ON attachments(organization_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_campaigns_org        ON campaigns(organization_id);

-- ── Uniqueness per organization ─────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Constraint names are the PostgreSQL defaults from V1 (<table>_<column>_key).
ALTER TABLE recipients DROP CONSTRAINT recipients_email_key;
ALTER TABLE recipients ADD CONSTRAINT uq_recipients_org_email UNIQUE (organization_id, email);

ALTER TABLE unsubscribe_list DROP CONSTRAINT unsubscribe_list_email_key;
ALTER TABLE unsubscribe_list ADD CONSTRAINT uq_unsubscribe_org_email UNIQUE (organization_id, email);
````
